note: Concept register only. Everything here is provisional and concept-local; canon is never minted in a concept register - the implementation audit adjudicates.

plan_owner_impacts.evidence: Directory-first Settings Home (search hero, single gated critical banner, compact attention block, twelve destination cards, subdued utility footer) plus the card-transfer motion contract: the pressed card is the only element that journeys into the domain header; everything else is a restrained directional slide, and reduced motion collapses the transfer to an instant cut.

In-stage settings rail appears at domain level (never on Home) for cross-domain jumps, and disappears entirely at narrow widths in favor of push navigation with a named Back - the shell Activity Bar is never overlaid.

The rev-2 canonical deep-link probe system.health.diagnostics-verbosity is absent from the 828-row PM2_INVENTORY; the closest real row is system.health.platform-diagnostics. Any plan text or harness that cites the old id needs the census corrected. The concept renders an honest not-found surface for stale addresses instead of a dead end.

All navigation flows through one dest grammar (home | dest/cat[/sub] | manager/id[/object[/tab]] | setting/id | all | copy | search/query) with focus rids for exact-row reveals; a cmd.settings.navigate {dest} family plus cmd.settings.search {query} covers every surface this concept exposes (see candidate-command-delta.json).

Installation cards render selected/shadowed/manual-only with the shadow note and the unknown-owner refusal inline; the ask-first Codex update and the Cursor CLI explicit official-source setup (host/environment choice, sign-in separate) are actions with truthful staged ops - success is never the installer exit code alone.

The models table renders context, modes (effort/fast from catalog evidence, never name-inferred), tool support, and requested-vs-effective routing with reasons, inside the provider object page rather than a global wall.

Accounts tab: per-account health words (Ready / Included usage used up / Not signed in / Signed in cannot invoke), sign-in ownership boundary note rendered verbatim from the shared resolver, priority/sticky/use-next in the Details drawer.
Server connections group renders address, version, reachability, last handshake, and the server-supplied catalog note with the scoped-token-reference boundary; reconnect is a staged op.

Copy Settings is a centered review-flow transaction over a dimmed workspace: source, categories with counts, preview (add/replace/unchanged/unavailable/conflict + item inspection + credential-by-reference note), restore point, atomic verified apply, receipt with working rollback; source and destination stay independent.

Managed-workspace scenario renders the whole safety domain read-only with managed chips and policy origin in row Details; the permissions manager renders the rules table and FileSafe floor as sections of one preference document.
Context & Instructions manager renders admitted/omitted-with-why tables and the instruction precedence chain as read-only evidence sections behind one manager destination, not as inline row noise.
Ten keystone traces registered in candidate-wiring-delta.json, all flagged concept_local_state.

settings_inventory_impacts.note: Referenced by the rev-2 harness contract as the canonical deep-link probe but absent from PM2_INVENTORY; system.health.platform-diagnostics is the nearest real row. Either re-mint the row or retire the probe id.

Only meaningful while a Glass theme is active; the store marks it unavailable otherwise. The inventory schema has no field for value-dependency between rows - candidate: availability_condition metadata.

Both validation-error fixture rows are advanced-tier. Any tiered presentation must surface hidden row states at the fold summary (this concept adds a validation-error flag on the collapsed Advanced disclosure) or errors silently disappear.

settings_schema_impacts.note: resolveRow's seven states (normal, managed, unavailable, restart-required, reconnect-required, changed-elsewhere, error) all render distinctly; the schema should make state + stateNote first-class rather than derived.

Inventory options are raw enum strings (custom, ask, for_session); the store humanizes multi-word tokens for valueLabel but not single words. A display_label per option would remove per-concept re-humanization.
Min/max live in a store-side BOUNDS table, not the inventory. Controls and validation both need them; they belong on the setting record.

command_id_impacts.pointer: See candidate-command-delta.json in this directory; no canon minted. Flags the navigate/search/copy families plus per-manager action ids that should resolve to the shared trigger registry rather than new verbs.

wiring_impacts.pointer: See candidate-wiring-delta.json: ten keystone traces (value set with validation, select via popup menu, copy preview/apply/rollback, provider action refusal, cursor-cli setup, deep-link landing, scenario mirror), all concept_local_state.

dry_component_impacts.pointer: See candidate-dry-delta.json for the per-family concretized/reused/not-exercised classification with anti-clone variance notes.

schema_event_storage_impacts.note: ObservableWork payloads (queued/running(phase)/terminal, determinate only with a real denominator) render directly in the op strip and the copy panel; the event schema is sufficient as-is and should be frozen.
Receipt + restore point + skipped counts + rolledBack flag is exactly what the receipt surface needs; rollback must re-emit a value batch event, which pm2-copy already does.
URL-applied scenario/fixtures are ephemeral (persist:false) but consumers read store.get(); an explicit activeScenario channel on the store would remove the _setSession mirror this concept installs.

migration_supersession_impacts.note: Managers are not slides; Waypoint has no prev/next affordance anywhere. Back is strictly one level out and names its target.
Project identity is context only; legacyScope metadata surfaces solely inside the row Details drawer as impact-analysis prose.

slint_port_impacts.note: One measured clone flying rect-to-rect maps to an animated proxy Rectangle above the page (x/y/width/height animations); settle is a Timer, never a transition-end event.
The All Settings window (absolute rows at i*52px inside a spacer canvas) maps 1:1 to a Slint ListView with fixed row height.
Collision-flipped fixed-position menus map to Slint PopupWindow with explicit placement logic; option state is a plain model.
view {kind, cat, sub, managerId, objectId, tab, query} is a flat struct; every render is a pure function of it plus the store - no DOM-geometry-derived semantics.

test_fixtures.proof: Home shows the setup banner, zero attention, 'Nothing has been changed yet'; managers render their real empty states (driver + boot-check).
Web provider rows unavailable with reasons; offline attention item leads the list (driver + boot-check).
Safety rows read-only with managed chips and origin in Details (driver).
Single Home banner stages the review; its action deep-links to m.lifecycle (driver + boot-check).
Row-level error notes plus a fold-summary flag when the failing row is inside the collapsed Advanced disclosure (driver).
Provider activity keeps cached entries visible with a refresh indicator (driver).
Copy receipt flips to 'Rolled back' with the restore point named; values restored exactly (driver).
All Settings totals 2,828 with synthetic rows marked 'Stress fixture'; live DOM stays under 80 rows while scrolling (driver).

unresolved_questions: Should the single Home banner ever stack (e.g. import conflict during usage exhaustion)? This concept picks the first scenario/fixture notice and keeps the rest in the attention list - is that the product rule?

When a search result's destination is a reserved owner shell (u: capability under m.servers), is landing on the shell head with the availability reason the canonical behavior, or should the shell grow per-host anchor rows before its owner module lands?
Does the advanced-tier fold need a product-wide contract for surfacing hidden row states (error vs pending vs managed), or is per-concept judgment acceptable?
